view: Last week's fall was idiosyncratic. This week's was mostly sector-wide: SOX fell 17.1% and the S&P 500 8.6%. NVDA still lagged SOX by another 5.8 points and set a new low in NVDA/SOX (14.93, down 18.4% over 13 weeks and 46.5% over 52 weeks). The relative trend is still falling and shows no turn. A beat-and-fall earnings print followed by an SEC accounting headline points to the underperformance continuing. Because NVDA has high beta, the tails are wide in both directions. Tactical: Wait until NVDA/SOX stops making new lows.

probabilities.defs: vs price_at_call 125.53 (Fri 2026-11-20 close). next_2_weeks: up = close > 131.81 (+5%), down = close < 119.25 (-5%), range in between, measured at the close on or before 2026-12-06 (Fri 2026-12-04). this_quarter (close of 2026-12-31) and next_quarter (close of 2027-03-31): up > 138.08 (+10%), down < 112.98 (-10%), range in between. up + range + down = 100.

evidence.point: Week of 2026-11-16: NVDA -22.92%, SOX -17.13%, SPX -8.61%, Nasdaq Composite about -10% (its worst week since March 2020). Unlike last week, when SOX rose while NVDA fell, the whole sector and the index sold off hard. This week was mostly a sector and market event.

NVDA still lagged SOX by 5.8 points this week. On beta_vs_spx_59w 1.94, an S&P 500 fall of 8.61% implies about -16.7% for NVDA. The actual -22.9% leaves roughly 6 points of NVDA-specific loss against either benchmark. That is a smaller idiosyncratic gap than last week's 21.6 points against SOX, but it has not closed and is not reversing.

Friday 2026-11-20 (the SEC accounting report day): NVDA -14.01%, SOX -10.73%, AMD -13.25%, SPX -3.7%. An NVDA-specific headline cost NVDA only about 3.3 points more than SOX, and AMD fell almost as much. So Friday was mainly a de-risking of AI semis that NVDA's news set off or deepened, not NVDA alone.

NVDA/SOX is now 14.93, against 16.05 at last week's run, 18.29 13 weeks ago and 27.92 52 weeks ago. This is another lower weekly reading, so the relative downtrend that was already in place before the CEO exit is still running (13W -18.4%, 52W -46.5%).
NVDA/SPX: -35.1% over 13 weeks and -32.9% over 52 weeks. Most of the 52-week relative loss has come in the last quarter, so this is a recent, fast de-rating against the index, not a slow drift.

Rotation inside AI semis: weekly figures for AMD, AVGO, TSM and SMH are missing (page partial). Last week money moved from NVDA into AMD and AVGO. On Friday AMD fell 13.25% alongside NVDA, which suggests the peer refuge stopped working once the sector sold off. I cannot confirm whether the rotation continued or reversed over the week. This is unknown, not neutral.

Beta to SOX is 0.62 and correlation 0.64, up from 0.48 and 0.54 last week. NVDA is trading more with the sector again. Sector direction therefore matters more for NVDA's next two weeks than it did at the last run, in both directions.

Risk-off backdrop: VIX 35.9 (+26% on Friday), S5TH 45.9% of S&P 500 names above their 200-day average. When high-beta leaders lag in a broad drawdown, the oversold rebound is usually sharp but does not by itself repair relative strength. That is judgment, not data from the slice.

Outside view for 2W is 33 up / 45 range / 22 down. I cut range by 20 because daily ATR is 8.5% (structure.atr_daily_pct), so a ±5% close in two weeks is much easier than usual. I raised down by 18 for the new relative low, the close 0.8% above the session low and the unresolved SEC overhang, and up by 2 for oversold rebound potential. The ATR-driven tail-widening overlaps with the technical member's view: count it once.

After 2W drops of 15% or more (n=4), the 2W split was 50/50/0 and 100% of cases were up at 13W. After weekly RSI ≤36 (n=13), the 13W split was 69/0/31. Both samples are tiny and overlap. My judgment is that they are probably sector-wide washouts, not a single name carrying a CEO exit plus an SEC accounting question while lagging its sector. I moved next_quarter only from the 50/31/19 base to 42/23/35: up lower and down higher, because relative weakness plus a governance overhang argue against a clean mean reversion.

What relative strength usually does after a key-person shock: the slice has no analog data, so this is judgment only. Single-name governance shocks tend to keep underperforming until the uncertainty is resolved, because holders switch to peers instead of buying the dip. A second governance headline (here the SEC accounting report) usually extends that period. Before the 2026-11-17 print the relative signal was negative but could have been reset by a strong print. After it the print beat and the stock still fell, so fundamentals did not re-anchor the story. In relative-strength terms that is the more bearish outcome.

7/14 pages ok. tv_relative is partial (no peer or SMH weekly data), and the technicals pages, SEC filings and sentiment are stale. NVDA/SOX/SPX ratios and the weekly NVDA/SOX/SPX moves are present, so the core idiosyncratic-vs-sector call stands. The rotation call is blind, and options positioning is deferred, so I lowered confidence from 38 to 32.

key_levels.why: Low of the week and of Friday's session. Friday closed only 0.8% above it. A weekly close below it would extend the relative breakdown. The 200-week SMA sits about 1.1% below price (about 124.2, derived), so this is the long-term reference zone.
Quarterly down-bucket threshold (-10%). A close below it by 2026-12-04 while SOX falls less than 5% would mean the idiosyncratic de-rating is speeding up again.
Friday's high and the bottom of the gap 143.725-145.71 left by the SEC headline. Closing that gap would mean the market has priced out the accounting-specific part of the loss.
NVDA/SOX ratio now. The relative trend turns only after two weekly readings that do not set a new low; one up week inside a sector bounce is not enough.

what_would_change_my_mind: Expected: weekly closes on 2026-11-27 and 2026-12-04, and the next results in late Feb 2027 (inside the next_quarter window, a binary event). What matters is the outcome: whether NVDA/SOX stops falling.

NVDA beats SOX by 3 points or more in the week ending 2026-11-27 and again in the week ending 2026-12-04 (the NVDA/SOX ratio holds above 14.93): the idiosyncratic discount would be starting to unwind. I would move 2W to about 42 up / 22 range / 36 down and next_quarter up to about 50.
NVDA closes above 138.08 (+10%) on or before 2026-12-04 (2W +10% was reached in 26.1% of past windows) while beating SOX: relative repair. Raise up in all horizons.

NVDA closes below 112.98 (-10%) on or before 2026-12-04 (2W -10% was reached in 17.5% of past windows) in a week when SOX falls less than 5%: the governance discount is widening on its own. Raise 2W down to about 50 and next_quarter down to about 42.

SOX rebounds 5% or more in a week before 2026-12-04 while NVDA lags it by 3 points or more: the sector recovers without NVDA, which confirms a stock-specific overhang. Shift about 5 points from up to down in this_quarter and next_quarter.
notes_for_chair: Ladder (proposal only, owner's approval required; no orders): relative strength argues for slower pacing, not front-loading into the drawdown. I propose that deeper rungs need a relative condition as well as a price level, for example NVDA/SOX not making a new low for two weekly closes, so the ladder does not average into a still-active single-name de-rating. If the chair keeps price-only rungs, the reference zone from my slice is 124.5 (week low) to the 200-week SMA about 1.1% below price, with 112.98 as the next marker. That is a context level, not a support signal. The ladder's actual rung prices are not in my slice.

Cross-lane: the Reuters report that SEC enforcement staff are examining potential accounting issues does not fit TB1-TB4 as written (TB1 is export violations, TB2 is a CEO departure under legal pressure). The narrative/governance member should rule on whether it links to TB2 (the CEO exit). The owner may want a proposed accounting/restatement thesis break. That is a proposal for the owner only, not something I can apply.

Data inconsistency: NVDA weekly is -22.92% close to close (162.85 to 125.53), but the TradingView panel shows Perf.W -26.12%. That is probably a different reference window. Use -22.92%. My NVDA-SOX gap of 5.8 points is based on the close-to-close figure.
Unclear item in tv_relative: 'anthropic_d -8.5' has no clear ticker or meaning, so I have not used it.

TB4 context: the sector-wide fall (SOX -17%) is consistent with either general risk-off (VIX 35.9, Fed-hike talk in macro) or a capex scare. My slice cannot tell which. The capex member should check hyperscaler_capex; nothing in my data shows a guidance cut.
Overlap: the ATR-driven tail-widening and the oversold base rates are the momentum/technical group. Count them once.

Pre-mortem: if this is badly wrong in three months, the most likely reason is that the SEC matter fades quickly and a sector rebound with NVDA's 1.94 beta to the S&P 500 lifts it well above 138.08, as the small n=4 conditional sample suggests. My relative-strength discount would then have been anchoring on last week's idiosyncratic story.
